name: NextEra Energy

header.one_liner: America's largest clean-energy developer plus a Florida utility, about to absorb Dominion; 8%+ EPS growth at 21x.
header.thesis: NextEra grew adjusted EPS 9.7% in the third quarter, with Florida Power & Light earnings up about 11% and the renewables and storage backlog at 36.7 GW. It agreed in May to buy Dominion Energy in an all-stock deal expected to close in the second half of 2027, which raises its regulated growth target. The plan is credible; the price pays for most of it.

base.eps_label: FY2026E adjusted EPS: top of the $3.92 to $4.02 guidance range, which management is targeting
base.rev_label: FY2026E operating revenues ($B), near consensus; reported revenue swings with derivative marks

rev_cagr.why: Management targets adjusted EPS growth of 8% or more a year through 2032 off a 2025 base of $3.71. FPL's regulatory capital employed grew 9.2% and the backlog is 36.7 GW. The base case grows revenue about 9% a year on a standalone basis; the Dominion deal is not modelled until it closes.

margin_end.why: Adjusted net margin is about 27% of revenue. The base case holds it flat: rate-base growth at FPL is steady, while NEER margins depend on tax credits and contract prices.

share_chg.why: NextEra funds growth partly with equity and equity units, adding about 1% to the share count a year. The Dominion deal would issue about 0.81 NextEra shares per Dominion share at close, but also adds Dominion's earnings, so it is left out of this standalone model.

exit_pe.why: Today's multiple is about 21x 2026 adjusted EPS, above Duke and Southern. The base case assumes a small de-rating toward the regulated-utility range while the merger is pending.
exit_pe.source: Engine judgment; peer multiples from the Moat Monitor peer table

pillars.title: Both businesses are growing
pillars.claim: Adjusted EPS rose 9.7% to $1.24: FPL net income up about 11% and NEER adjusted earnings up about 13%.

evidence.t: Adjusted earnings $2.592B vs $2.348B; FPL net income $1.62B vs $1.463B

pillars.test: Does adjusted EPS land at the top of the $3.92 to $4.02 range?

pillars.title: The backlog keeps filling
pillars.claim: NEER added 3.7 GW in the quarter, including 2.4 GW of battery storage; the backlog is about 36.7 GW.

evidence.t: 1.8 GW placed in service since July

pillars.test: Do additions stay above 3 GW a quarter as tax credits phase down?

pillars.title: Dominion changes the company
pillars.claim: An all-stock merger, 0.8138 NextEra shares per Dominion share, expected to close in the second half of 2027.

evidence.t: Shareholders of both companies approved on 3 September; Virginia and South Carolina orders expected January 2027

pillars.test: Do the state commissions approve without heavy conditions?

pillars.title: Data centers are a new channel
pillars.claim: Federal hub projects totalling about 16.5 GW and a planned Paducah campus point to large-load growth.

evidence.t: $5.7B of initial funding secured for hub projects year to date

pillars.test: Do data center contracts convert into owned, regulated or contracted assets?

variant.street: The market pays about 21x 2026 adjusted EPS for 8%+ growth and the largest clean-energy pipeline in the US.
variant.ours: The growth plan is credible and the Dominion deal adds regulated rate base. Our base case grows EPS about 8% a year and lets the multiple drift slightly, which earns about the cost of equity.
variant.could_be_wrong: If data center demand turns the backlog into faster growth and the merger closes cleanly, 9%+ growth supports a higher multiple.
variant.would_change_mind: Merger approval with heavy conditions, or backlog additions below 2 GW a quarter.

arguments.label: Growth
arguments.text: Adjusted EPS grew 9.7% in the third quarter, with Florida Power & Light up about 11%. The backlog is 36.7 GW and management targets 8%+ EPS growth a year through 2032.

thesis_long: NextEra combines Florida's largest regulated utility with the largest developer of wind, solar and storage in North America. Both are growing: adjusted EPS rose 9.7% in the third quarter, FPL's capital employed grew 9.2%, and the renewables and storage backlog reached 36.7 GW after 3.7 GW of additions. Data center demand is adding a new channel through federal hub projects and owned generation.

In May NextEra agreed to buy Dominion Energy for about 0.81 NextEra shares per Dominion share, adding regulated utilities in Virginia and the Carolinas. Shareholders have approved; state commissions decide from January 2027 and closing is expected in the second half of 2027. The combined company targets 9%+ EPS growth, but the deal brings approval risk and more leverage to a company already at about 6.7 times EBITDA.

Our standalone base case grows EPS about 8% a year with a small de-rating from 21x, which earns about the cost of equity over 12 months. We would turn positive on a clean merger approval with data center contracts converting into owned assets, and negative on heavy merger conditions or backlog additions below 2 GW a quarter.

upside_risks.how: Approval without heavy conditions in January would remove the main overhang and support the 9%+ combined growth target.
Converting hub projects and large-load contracts into owned assets would lift growth above the plan.
